chapter: Los Angeles: Roy Milton and Central Avenue
title: The Civic Hotel residents and comedian Willie Lewis
summary: Gene Montgomery and comedian Willie Lewis lived at the Civic Hotel, the funniest man he knew and a baton twirler.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: In the meantime, the tenor player from the band had left also, and he had come back to Los Angeles, Gene Montgomery -- because his father owned the poolroom downstairs under the Civic Hotel; and he lived in the hotel. And a lot of great people lived in and out of the Civic Hotel. I met a lot of great people.

That's where I first met...not the first time I met him, but he was living there...the great comedian, Willie Lewis. I had worked with him in Detroit when it was Spizzy and Willie. This guy was probably the funniest guy I ever heard, really. He had an incredible sense of humor. He never really got it big, but Redd Foxx and Slappy White, all those guys will tell who the best one was -- it was Willie Lewis. And he was the master baton twirler. He could put a hat over his face and twirl two batons, and do all kind of things with them, throwing them all kind of places and catching them with his face covered, you know! He was a spectacular guy. And in fact, he was a twenty-four-hour-a-day comedian. Every time you'd see him he was funny, without trying to be real funny, you know. But he had that kind of a mind, you know. He could say very stupid things were funny, you know...! [LAUGHS] We all worked with him later on sometimes.
